reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is to instruct viewers on setting up and budgeting a Google Ads campaign for IT or email-support calls. The expected calls, advertising budget, and broader IT-support webpage describe ordinary paid advertising, while the email/password-support wording and unverified suspension-avoidance statement do not by themselves establish deceptive intent, credential collection, payment demands, or harmful outcomes.

the budget. Should be 9500 rupees per day
You can see it is a normal website which is an IT support website. I have not mentioned anything related to email support or anything like that.

opening.argument: This is not merely neutral advertising instruction: it links a paid setup process to an easy operational outcome, namely generating incoming support calls. The viewer is told to configure a campaign, select keywords, set a daily budget, and then run it, with the promised result framed as calls arriving. That action-outcome pairing is especially concerning because the tutorial presents the process as straightforward and repeatable, while also positioning it as a way to avoid account consequences. The practical solicitation is to spend money and deploy the campaign in order to obtain calls from people searching for email and password help.

citations.quote: today in this video I will show how exactly you can generate email calls using. Google Adwords without any risk of suspension.
the budget. Should be 9500 rupees per day
you just need to run this ad and you. Will start getting calls.
as many keywords as you. Add so you have an increased probability of getting much calls

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an ordinary campaign tutorial does not answer the central linkage: the viewer is instructed to spend a stated daily amount and is told that running the ad will produce calls. The fact that Google Ads is used describes the mechanism, not whether the promised outcome or the promoted service is trustworthy. Nor does an absence of explicit payment demands eliminate a solicitation to fund and deploy the campaign.

citations.quote: the budget. Should be 9500 rupees per day
you just need to run this ad and you. Will start getting calls.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited instructions show campaign spending and an anticipated advertising result, but they do not show a free reward, cash return, or asset acquisition. “Calls” are prospective customer contacts, not a promised payout to the viewer. The material also does not establish that anyone was deceived or harmed merely because it explains how to buy ads and measure calls.

citations.quote: generate email calls using. Google Adwords
you. Will start getting calls.

opening.argument: Several concrete warning signals appear together. The speaker advertises a method of using Google Adwords “without any risk of suspension,” then builds an ad for email and password assistance while describing the destination as a general IT-support site that does not mention email support. The keyword strategy reaches people searching for password and email-reset help, and the proposed ad directs those users to a toll-free call. This combination makes the suspension-avoidance claim more significant: it is not an abstract marketing lesson, but a method for presenting a sensitive support service to account-access seekers while keeping the destination framing broader than the ad’s promise.

citations.quote: using. Google Adwords without any risk of suspension.
call helpline tool. Free in number 2 let's come to the second line because I don't have any. Other option to fix and reset email and password issues
You can see it is a normal website which is an IT support website. I have not mentioned anything related to email support or anything like that.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. It calls the website “normal,” but the tutorial itself emphasizes that email support is omitted from it, even as the ad targets email and password problems. Likewise, “without any risk of suspension” is not a harmless aside when the video is teaching a specific campaign configuration. The evidence need not show credential theft to establish a deceptive-looking mismatch and a rule-avoidance pitch.

citations.quote: without any risk of suspension.
I have not mentioned anything related to email support or anything like that.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These details may justify caution, but they still do not prove the claimed scam subtype. The ad’s password language can describe support inquiries, and a general IT-support site can provide broader services than the ad headline. The statement about suspension is unverified and potentially overconfident, but it does not itself establish a reward, asset, or fraudulent acquisition flow.

citations.quote: it is a normal website which is an IT support website
without any risk of suspension.

opening.argument: The instructional format functions as promotion because it repeatedly moves from explanation to deployment: choose the target countries, create the call ad, add keywords, and run it. The apparent lesson is therefore also a ready-made funnel for directing people with email or password problems toward a phone service. The presentation emphasizes approval, eligibility, more keywords, and the expectation of calls, which steers the viewer toward participation rather than neutrally examining whether the advertised support is genuine. The destination reinforces that promotional role by prominently asking people to call an IT-support number.

citations.quote: I have selected two countries for my ad
you have to type in your phone. Number your toll-free number
you will have. Much more focus on your audience

rebuttal.rebuttal: The label “tutorial” does not neutralize the promotional function. The video does not merely discuss advertising concepts; it demonstrates a live campaign, a phone number, sensitive search terms, approval status, and the steps needed to send callers to the service. Describing the process as operational education leaves unanswered why the lesson is built around promoting this particular support line and expanding its reach.

citations.quote: you will have. Much more focus on your audience
you just need to run this ad

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An operational demonstration can naturally include a sample phone ad and destination without becoming a scam. The evidence shows promotion of a service and instructions for purchasing search traffic, but not a deceptive reward or asset-acquisition promise. The website’s general IT-support description also supplies an ordinary commercial explanation for the call funnel, even if the ad’s email wording is narrower.
